newsitem.title: USA: Renegade tobacco exec tells jury cigarettes cause cancer.
newsitem.headline: Renegade tobacco exec tells jury cigarettes cause cancer.

text.p: The owner of cigarette-maker Liggett Group testified Monday in a landmark secondhand-smoke trial that smoking causes cancer and is addictive for many people.
Bennett LeBow, whose Brooke Group Ltd owns Liggett, one of the defendants in the secondhand-smoke trial, is the only U.S. tobacco chief executive to say publicly that smoking is a health hazard.
"...The answer is yes," LeBow said when asked by plaintiffs attorney Stanely Rosenblatt if cigarette smoking caused cancer.
"Yes, we believe that for many people smoking cigarettes is very addictive," LeBow said in response to another question.

In the past two years LeBow made separate agreements with anti-tobacco forces that were denounced by other cigarette makers but were later seen crucial in bringing about the tentative $368.5 billion settlement announced last month between tobacco companies and state attorneys general suing cigarette makers.
LeBow, whose company has only 2 percent of the U.S. cigarette market, was repeatedly interrupted by tobacco company lawyers.

The tobacco lawyers had secured a judge's ruling that LeBow may not mention the June settlement before the jurors hearing the $5 billion lawsuit on behalf of non-smoking airline flight attendants who say passengers' smoke harmed their health.
